serving.statement: ANALYSIS-ONLY: this lifestyle model is never served to users and has no API endpoint. It must not be used to make statements about any person.

data.notice: SYNTHETIC DATA: all 1,200 survey respondents are artificially generated; none are real people. Results reflect the data generator's rules, not real-world patterns, and are not real-world accuracy.
data.class_balance: 300 per class (Normal, Depression, Anxiety, Stress); gender and age-group mix identical in every class by construction

metrics_disclaimer: These metrics measure recovery of relationships the synthetic data generator simulated with assumed strengths. They are not real-world accuracy and must not be reported as such.
task: Predict the dataset's Emotional_State label (derived from DASS-21 answers) from lifestyle answers only.

feature_notes.bmi: weight_kg / (height_cm / 100)^2, computed by make_X before the pipeline

exclusion_reason: Emotional_State is computed from q1..q21; items, scores and severities would leak the label.

evaluation.protocol: outer stratified 5-fold CV (one row per respondent); inner stratified 3-fold grid search on macro-F1; preprocessing fit inside training folds only

limitations: Data are fully synthetic; relationships and their strengths are the generator author's assumptions.
mindless_snacking options 'Due to Stress' and 'Due to Anxity' name the target classes; any signal there is self-description, not an independent lifestyle effect.

Gender and age-group mixes are identical in every class by design, so neither predicts the class on its own; age group can still matter in combination with other features (e.g. under-18 rows are set to non-smoker / non-drinker), which is what its permutation importance reflects.
Not validated on any real population.
ethics: No output of this model is a diagnosis, screening result or statement about a person. DASS-21 screening results for users come only from scoring.py applied to their own answers.
